title: Elapsed Time: Units of Time, Start and End Times, and Schedules
seo_title: Grade 4 Elapsed Time Worksheets: Hours and Minutes, a.m. and p.m., Schedules (Free Math, Answer Key)
standard_text: Solve problems involving elapsed time by applying the relationships between different units of time
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on elapsed time for the Ontario curriculum: seconds, minutes, hours, days and weeks, clocks to the minute with a.m. and p.m., elapsed time across hours, start and end times, and schedules for hockey practice and a road trip. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count on in jumps: to the next o’clock, then whole hours, then the minutes left.
key_sub: 1 hour = 60 minutes, not 100, so do not subtract clock times like ordinary numbers. 1 minute = 60 seconds, 1 day = 24 hours and 1 week = 7 days. After 12 noon, times are p.m.
body_html:
Units of time

Time does not count in tens and hundreds. Learn these facts:

Bigger unitIs the same as
1 minute60 seconds
1 hour60 minutes
1 day24 hours
1 week7 days

To change a bigger unit into a smaller one, multiply: 3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes. To change minutes into hours, take away 60 for each hour: 150 minutes = 60 + 60 + 30 = 2 hours 30 minutes.

Clocks to the minute, a.m. and p.m.

The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes: count by 5s to the last number, then by 1s. a.m. times are from midnight to noon. p.m. times are from noon to midnight.

Elapsed time: count on in jumps

Elapsed time is how much time passes from a start time to an end time. Draw a time line. Jump to the next o’clock, then jump whole hours, then jump the minutes that are left. Add the jumps.

Example 1: within the hour

Recess is from 10:20 a.m. to 10:35 a.m. How long is it?

Both times are in the same hour: 35 − 20 = 15.

Answer: 15 minutes

Example 2: across an hour

Skating is from 3:50 p.m. to 4:20 p.m. How long is it?

3:50 to 4:00 is 10 minutes. 4:00 to 4:20 is 20 minutes. 10 + 20 = 30.

Answer: 30 minutes (not 70 minutes)

Finding the end time or the start time

To find an end time, add: first the hours, then the minutes. To find a start time, count back. Watch for 12 noon: times after noon are p.m.

Example 3: end time

A movie starts at 6:50 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 45 minutes. When does it end?

Add 1 hour: 6:50 p.m. → 7:50 p.m. Then add 45 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 35 minutes more is 8:35 p.m.

Answer: 8:35 p.m.

Example 4: start time

Lunch is ready at 12:20 p.m. It cooked for 35 minutes. When did it start?

Count back 35 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 15 minutes more is 11:45 a.m. Going back past noon changes p.m. to a.m.

Answer: 11:45 a.m.

Reading a schedule

A schedule lists start and end times. Find the two times you need, then count on.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3:50 to 4:20 worked out as 420 − 350 = 70 minutesAn hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on: 10 + 20 = 30 minutes
1 hour 15 minutes = 115 minutes1 hour = 60 minutes: 60 + 15 = 75 minutes
11:50 a.m. + 40 minutes = 12:30 a.m.After 12 noon the time is p.m.: 12:30 p.m.
9:45 + 30 minutes = 9:15 (forgot the new hour)45 + 30 = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes, so it is 10:15
3 days = 36 hours1 day = 24 hours, not 12: 3 × 24 = 72 hours
Adding to find a start timeCount back from the end time

faq.q: What do Grade 4 students learn about elapsed time in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum (expectation E2.3), Grade 4 students solve problems about elapsed time using the relationships between seconds, minutes, hours, days and weeks.

faq.q: What is the easiest way to teach elapsed time?
faq.a: Use an open time line and count on in jumps: to the next o’clock, then whole hours, then the minutes left. Adding the jumps is easier and safer than subtracting the times.

faq.q: Why can’t you subtract times like ordinary numbers?
faq.a: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. So 4:20 − 3:50 is not 70 minutes; counting on gives 10 + 20 = 30 minutes.

faq.q: What time facts should a Grade 4 student know?
faq.a: 60 seconds = 1 minute, 60 minutes = 1 hour, 24 hours = 1 day and 7 days = 1 week. They should also know that a.m. is from midnight to noon and p.m. is from noon to midnight.

sets.title: Units of time: seconds, minutes, hours, days and weeks

items.q: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
items.e: There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)

items.q: How many seconds are in 1 minute?
items.e: There are 60 seconds in 1 minute, just like 60 minutes in 1 hour.

items.q: How many hours are in 1 day?
items.e: A day is 24 hours: 12 hours of a.m. and 12 hours of p.m. 12 + 12 = 24. (Not 12: the clock goes around twice in one day.)

items.q: How many days are in 1 week?
items.e: A week has 7 days: Monday to Sunday. (5 is only the school days.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to tell how long March Break lasts?
items.e: March Break is more than a week long. We count it in days (9 days with the weekends).

items.q: About how long does a car trip from Toronto to Ottawa take?
items.e: Toronto and Ottawa are about 450 km apart. Driving on the highway takes about 5 hours. 5 minutes is far too short, and 5 days is far too long.

items.q: 3 minutes = ? seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 3 × 60 = 180 seconds. (300 counts a minute as 100 seconds. 63 adds 60 + 3 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: 2 hours = ? minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 2 × 60 = 120 minutes. (200 counts an hour as 100 minutes. 48 uses 24, but 24 is the hours in a day.)

items.q: 5 weeks = ? days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 5 × 7 = 35 days. (25 counts only the 5 school days in each week.)

items.q: 3 days = ? hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. 3 × 24 = 72 hours. (36 uses 12 hours in a day. 180 uses 60.)

items.q: 180 seconds = ?
items.e: 60 seconds = 1 minute. 60 + 60 + 60 = 180, so 180 seconds = 3 minutes. (1 minute 80 seconds counts a minute as 100 seconds.)

items.q: 1 hour 15 minutes = ? minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 + 15 = 75 minutes. (115 counts an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: Amira’s hockey practice lasts 1 hour 30 minutes. How many minutes is that?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 + 30 = 90 minutes. (130 counts an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: 2 minutes 30 seconds = ? seconds
items.e: 2 minutes = 2 × 60 = 120 seconds. 120 + 30 = 150 seconds. (230 counts a minute as 100 seconds.)

items.q: Zoe goes to summer camp for 2 weeks. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 2 × 7 = 14 days. (10 days counts only school days. 9 adds 2 + 7.)

items.q: 21 days = ?
items.e: 7 days make 1 week. 7 + 7 + 7 = 21, so 21 days = 3 weeks. (4 weeks 1 day uses 5 days in a week.)

items.q: 10 days = ?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 10 − 7 = 3 days left. So 10 days = 1 week 3 days. (1 week 5 days is 12 days.)

items.q: 150 minutes = ?
items.e: 60 + 60 = 120 minutes make 2 hours. 150 − 120 = 30 minutes left. So 150 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. (1 hour 50 minutes counts an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: Which is longer: 90 minutes or 1 hour 20 minutes?
items.e: 1 hour 20 minutes = 60 + 20 = 80 minutes. 90 is more than 80, so 90 minutes is longer. (1 hour 20 minutes is not 120 minutes.)

items.q: Which is longer: 3 days or 70 hours?
items.e: 3 days = 3 × 24 = 72 hours. 72 is more than 70, so 3 days is longer, by 2 hours.

sets.title: Clocks to the minute, a.m. and p.m.

items.e: The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 4. Count by 5s to 20, then by 1s: 23 minutes. So the time is 8:23. (Not 8:20: count the small marks after the 4 too.)

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 46 minutes. It is before noon, so it is a.m. The time is 11:46 a.m. (Not 11:46 p.m.: that is at night.)

items.q: Which time is later in the same day: 10:50 a.m. or 2:05 p.m.?
items.e: a.m. times come before noon and p.m. times come after noon. So 2:05 p.m. is later, even though 10 is bigger than 2.

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4. It has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is 3. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 49 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. The time is 3:49 p.m. (Not 3:49 a.m.: that is in the middle of the night.)

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6. It has not reached 6 yet, so the hour is 5. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 3. Count by 5s to 15, then by 1s: 19 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. The time is 5:19 p.m. (Not 5:19 a.m.: that is in the middle of the night.)
The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 12: 2 minutes. So the time is 11:02.

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 47 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. The time is 6:47 p.m. (Not 6:47 a.m.: that is in the morning.)
At 2:36 the long hand is 1 small mark past the 7, and the short hand is between 2 and 3, close to 3. That is clock D. (Clock A shows 3:36; clock B shows 2:24; clock C shows 2:07.)

items.q: Write 17 minutes past 9 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “17 minutes past 9” means 17 minutes after 9 o’clock. It is in the morning, so the time is 9:17 a.m.

items.q: Write 18 minutes to 4 in the afternoon as a digital time.
items.e: “18 minutes to 4” means 18 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 18 = 42, so it is 42 minutes past 3. It is in the afternoon, so the time is 3:42 p.m.

items.q: A digital clock shows 6:38 p.m. How many minutes is it until 7:00 p.m.?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. 60 − 38 = 22 minutes. (Not 62: that is 100 − 38, but an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 48 − 5 = 43 minutes.
Both times are in the same hour: 50 − 12 = 38 minutes.

items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 34 − 7 = 27 minutes.

items.q: Lunch is from 11:45 a.m. to 12:25 p.m. How long is lunch?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 11:45 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 15 minutes; 12:00 noon to 12:25 p.m. is 25 minutes. 15 minutes + 25 minutes = 40 minutes. (Not 80 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Ethan skates at the rink from 3:50 p.m. to 4:20 p.m. How long does he skate?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 3:50 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 10 minutes; 4:00 p.m. to 4:20 p.m. is 20 minutes. 10 minutes + 20 minutes = 30 minutes. (Not 70 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Gym class is from 9:35 a.m. to 10:10 a.m. How long is gym class?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 9:35 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 10:10 a.m. is 10 minutes. 25 minutes + 10 minutes = 35 minutes. (Not 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Leah’s swimming lesson is from 5:40 p.m. to 6:15 p.m. How long is it?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 5:40 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 20 minutes; 6:00 p.m. to 6:15 p.m. is 15 minutes. 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 35 minutes. (Not 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Banana bread bakes in the oven from 2:48 p.m. to 3:41 p.m. How long does it bake?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 2:48 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 12 minutes; 3:00 p.m. to 3:41 p.m. is 41 minutes. 12 minutes + 41 minutes = 53 minutes. (Not 93 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)
Count on in jumps: 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 2 hours; 4:00 p.m. to 4:45 p.m. is 45 minutes. 2 hours + 45 minutes = 2 hours 45 minutes.

items.q: A movie starts at 6:45 p.m. and ends at 8:30 p.m. How long is the movie?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 6:45 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 15 minutes; 7:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 1 hour; 8:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. is 30 minutes. 1 hour + 15 minutes + 30 minutes = 1 hour 45 minutes. (Not 1 hour 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: The field trip bus leaves at 9:20 a.m. and gets to the museum at 11:05 a.m. How long is the ride?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 9:20 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 40 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 1 hour; 11:00 a.m. to 11:05 a.m. is 5 minutes. 1 hour + 40 minutes + 5 minutes = 1 hour 45 minutes. (Not 1 hour 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Kai and Noah go on a canoe trip from 8:15 a.m. to 12:00 noon. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 8:15 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 45 minutes; 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 3 hours. 3 hours + 45 minutes = 3 hours 45 minutes. (Not 3 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: The Terry Fox Run at school goes from 10:50 a.m. to 12:35 p.m. How long is it?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 10:50 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 10 minutes; 11:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 1 hour; 12:00 noon to 12:35 p.m. is 35 minutes. 1 hour + 10 minutes + 35 minutes = 1 hour 45 minutes. (Not 1 hour 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Aiden’s family drives to the cottage from 1:35 p.m. to 4:10 p.m. How long is the drive?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 1:35 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 25 minutes; 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 2 hours; 4:00 p.m. to 4:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 25 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 35 minutes. (Not 2 hours 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: The maple syrup festival is open from 9:40 a.m. to 1:10 p.m. How long is it open?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 9:40 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 20 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 3 hours; 1:00 p.m. to 1:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 3 hours + 20 minutes + 10 minutes = 3 hours 30 minutes.

items.q: A soccer tournament runs from 10:30 a.m. to 2:15 p.m. How long is the tournament?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 10:30 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 30 minutes; 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 3 hours; 2:00 p.m. to 2:15 p.m. is 15 minutes. 3 hours + 30 minutes + 15 minutes = 3 hours 45 minutes.

items.q: A class visits the science centre from 9:55 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. How long is the visit?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 9:55 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 5 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 4 hours; 2:00 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. is 30 minutes. 4 hours + 5 minutes + 30 minutes = 4 hours 35 minutes.

items.q: School starts at 8:45 a.m. and ends at 3:20 p.m. How long is the school day?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon. Count on in jumps: 8:45 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 15 minutes; 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 6 hours; 3:00 p.m. to 3:20 p.m. is 20 minutes. 6 hours + 15 minutes + 20 minutes = 6 hours 35 minutes.

sets.title: Finding the start time or the end time

items.q: Recess starts at 10:20 a.m. It lasts 15 minutes. What time does recess end?
items.e: Add 15 minutes: 10:35 a.m.

items.q: The school bus leaves at 8:25 a.m. The ride takes 30 minutes. What time does it get to school?
items.e: Add 30 minutes: 8:55 a.m.

items.q: Jayden goes to bed at 8:30 p.m. He reads for 20 minutes before bed. What time does he start reading?
items.e: Count back 20 minutes: 8:10 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 8:30 p.m.)

items.q: Art class starts at 1:35 p.m. It lasts 40 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 40 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 2:00 p.m., and 15 minutes more is 2:15 p.m.

items.q: Olivia starts reading at 7:45 p.m. and reads for 25 minutes. What time does she stop?
items.e: Add 25 minutes: 15 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 10 minutes more is 8:10 p.m.

items.q: Hana’s soccer game starts at 6:10 p.m. She leaves home 25 minutes before the game. What time does she leave?
items.e: Count back 25 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 6:00 p.m., and 15 minutes more is 5:45 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 6:10 p.m.)

items.q: Emma’s swimming lesson starts at 4:40 p.m. It lasts 55 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 55 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 5:00 p.m., and 35 minutes more is 5:35 p.m.

items.q: School starts at 8:45 a.m. Sofia’s walk to school takes 18 minutes. What time must she leave home?
items.e: Count back 18 minutes: 8:27 a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 8:45 a.m.)

items.q: Lunch starts at 11:50 a.m. It lasts 40 minutes. What time does lunch end?
items.e: Add 40 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 30 minutes more is 12:30 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

items.q: The pizza is ready at 12:20 p.m. It baked for 35 minutes. What time did it go in the oven?
items.e: Count back 35 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 15 minutes more is 11:45 a.m. Counting back past 12 noon changes p.m. to a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 12:20 p.m.)

items.q: A movie starts at 6:50 p.m. It lasts 1 hour 45 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 6:50 p.m. → 7:50 p.m. Then add 45 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 35 minutes more is 8:35 p.m.

items.q: The field trip bus leaves at 9:15 a.m. The ride takes 1 hour 50 minutes. What time does the bus arrive?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 9:15 a.m. → 10:15 a.m. Then add 50 minutes: 45 minutes takes you to 11:00 a.m., and 5 minutes more is 11:05 a.m.

items.q: A concert ends at 3:05 p.m. It lasted 50 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 50 minutes: 5 minutes takes you to 3:00 p.m., and 45 minutes more is 2:15 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 3:05 p.m.)

items.q: A movie ends at 9:05 p.m. It lasted 1 hour 40 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 1 hour: 9:05 p.m. → 8:05 p.m. Then count back 40 minutes: 5 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 35 minutes more is 7:25 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 9:05 p.m.)

items.q: Early hockey practice ends at 7:30 a.m. It lasted 1 hour 15 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 1 hour: 7:30 a.m. → 6:30 a.m. Then count back 15 minutes: 6:15 a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 7:30 a.m.)

items.q: Bread rises from 2:20 p.m. for 100 minutes. What time is it ready?
items.e: 100 minutes is not 1 hour: 100 = 60 + 40, so it is 1 hour 40 minutes. Add 1 hour: 2:20 p.m. → 3:20 p.m. Then add 40 minutes: 4:00 p.m. (3:20 p.m. counts 100 minutes as 1 hour.)

items.q: On Thanksgiving, the turkey goes in the oven at 11:30 a.m. It cooks for 3 hours 15 minutes. What time is it ready?
items.e: Add 3 hours: 11:30 a.m. → 2:30 p.m. Then add 15 minutes: 2:45 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

items.q: A soccer tournament starts at 10:45 a.m. It lasts 2 hours 30 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 2 hours: 10:45 a.m. → 12:45 p.m. Then add 30 minutes: 15 minutes takes you to 1:00 p.m., and 15 minutes more is 1:15 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

items.q: Mei’s family gets to the cottage at 1:10 p.m. The drive took 2 hours 25 minutes. What time did they leave home?
items.e: Count back 2 hours: 1:10 p.m. → 11:10 a.m. Then count back 25 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 11:00 a.m., and 15 minutes more is 10:45 a.m. Counting back past 12 noon changes p.m. to a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 1:10 p.m.)

items.q: A canoe trip starts at 8:40 a.m. It lasts 3 hours 35 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 3 hours: 8:40 a.m. → 11:40 a.m. Then add 35 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 15 minutes more is 12:15 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

sets.title: Schedules and word problems: hockey practice and a road trip

items.q: How long are the skating drills?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 50 − 15 = 35 minutes.

items.q: How long is the whole practice, from the start of the warm-up to the end of the scrimmage?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 1 hour; 10:00 a.m. to 10:45 a.m. is 45 minutes. 1 hour + 45 minutes = 1 hour 45 minutes.

items.q: Chloe gets to the rink 20 minutes before the warm-up starts. What time does she get there?
items.e: Count back 20 minutes: 8:40 a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 9:00 a.m.)

items.q: Which part of the practice is the longest?
items.e: Warm-up: 15 minutes. Skating drills: 9:15 to 9:50 is 35 minutes. Passing drills: 10 minutes to 10:00, then 20 more: 30 minutes. Scrimmage: 25 minutes. The longest is skating drills. (Passing drills are not 70 minutes: 1020 − 950 counts an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: Mateo’s family stays at the cottage for 2 weeks 3 days. How many days is that?
items.e: 2 weeks = 2 × 7 = 14 days. 14 + 3 = 17 days. (13 uses 5 days in a week. 23 uses 10 days in a week.)

items.q: Priya’s family goes camping for 72 hours. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. 24 + 24 + 24 = 72, so 72 hours = 3 days. (6 days uses 12 hours in a day.)

items.q: The Terry Fox Run starts at 10:40 a.m. Maya finishes 48 minutes later. What time does she finish?
items.e: Add 48 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 11:00 a.m., and 28 minutes more is 11:28 a.m.

items.q: How long is the drive from Toronto to Kingston?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 8:35 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 2 hours; 11:00 a.m. to 11:05 a.m. is 5 minutes. 2 hours + 25 minutes + 5 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. (Not 2 hours 70 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: How long does the family stop in Kingston?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 50 − 5 = 45 minutes.

items.q: How long is the drive from Kingston to Ottawa?
items.e: The drive goes past 12 noon, so jump to noon on the way. Count on in jumps: 11:50 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 10 minutes; 12:00 noon to 1:00 p.m. is 1 hour; 1:00 p.m. to 1:55 p.m. is 55 minutes. 1 hour + 10 minutes + 55 minutes = 2 hours 5 minutes. (10 minutes + 55 minutes = 65 minutes = 1 hour 5 minutes.) (Not 9 hours 55 minutes: 1:55 p.m. is after 11:50 a.m., not before it.)

items.q: How long is the whole trip, from leaving Toronto to arriving in Ottawa?
items.e: The trip goes past 12 noon. Count on in jumps: 8:35 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 4 hours; 1:00 p.m. to 1:55 p.m. is 55 minutes. 4 hours + 25 minutes + 55 minutes = 5 hours 20 minutes. (25 minutes + 55 minutes = 80 minutes = 1 hour 20 minutes.) (4 hours 35 minutes is only the driving time. The whole trip also has the stop.)

items.q: How much of the trip is spent driving?
items.e: Toronto to Kingston: 2 hours 30 minutes. Kingston to Ottawa: 2 hours 5 minutes. 2 hours + 2 hours = 4 hours, and 30 + 5 = 35 minutes. The driving time is 4 hours 35 minutes. (5 hours 20 minutes is the whole trip with the 45-minute stop.)

items.q: Ava has hockey practice 3 times a week. Each practice is 1 hour 15 minutes. How much practice is that in one week?
items.e: 3 × 1 hour = 3 hours. 3 × 15 minutes = 45 minutes. Together: 3 hours 45 minutes. (3 hours 15 minutes forgets to multiply the minutes by 3.)

items.q: Benjamin’s ringette practice is 1 hour 20 minutes. Arjun’s swim practice is 95 minutes. Whose practice is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 1 hour 20 minutes = 60 + 20 = 80 minutes. 95 − 80 = 15. So Arjun’s practice is longer, by 15 minutes. (Benjamin’s by 25 minutes counts an hour as 100 minutes: 120 − 95 = 25.)

items.q: Nathan practises piano for 25 minutes every day for 1 week. How long is that in all?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 7 × 25 = 175 minutes. 175 − 60 − 60 = 55, so 175 minutes = 2 hours 55 minutes. (1 hour 75 minutes counts an hour as 100 minutes. 2 hours 5 minutes uses only 5 days.)

items.q: Lucas’s family leaves for the cottage at 7:50 a.m. The drive takes 4 hours 25 minutes. What time do they arrive?
items.e: Add 4 hours: 7:50 a.m. → 11:50 a.m. Then add 25 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 15 minutes more is 12:15 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

items.q: A ringette game starts at 6:50 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 15 minutes. Then Owen’s family drives 20 minutes home. What time do they get home?
items.e: Game: 6:50 p.m. + 1 hour = 7:50 p.m., + 15 minutes = 8:05 p.m. Drive: 8:05 p.m. + 20 minutes = 8:25 p.m. (8:05 p.m. is when the game ends, before the drive.)

items.q: On a canoe trip, a class paddles until 12:10 p.m. They stop for lunch for 40 minutes. Then they paddle for 1 hour 25 minutes more. What time do they finish?
items.e: Lunch: 12:10 p.m. + 40 minutes = 12:50 p.m. Paddling: 12:50 p.m. + 1 hour = 1:50 p.m., + 10 minutes = 2:00 p.m., + 15 minutes = 2:15 p.m. (1:35 p.m. forgets the lunch stop.)

items.q: At a hockey tournament, a team plays 3 games. Each game lasts 1 hour, and there is a 45-minute break between games. The first game starts at 9:00 a.m. What time does the last game end?
items.e: Game 1: 9:00 to 10:00. Break: to 10:45. Game 2: to 11:45. Break: to 12:30 p.m. Game 3: to 1:30 p.m. There are only 2 breaks, because the breaks are between games. (12:00 noon forgets the breaks. 2:15 p.m. adds 3 breaks.)

items.q: Liam’s family goes on a 10-day road trip. Day 1 is a Saturday. On what day of the week is day 10?
items.e: A week is 7 days, so day 8 is a Saturday again. Day 9 is Sunday and day 10 is Monday. (Tuesday is 10 days after day 1, which would be day 11.)
